plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Primary gain direction/magnitude and response lag, which determine all subsequent safe steps and controller sizing.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.08 toward 0.3-0.5 over 180s with visible lag of tens of seconds and positive end-slope indicating not yet settled.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Time constant and steady-state gain for u=0.5 by observing settling; needed to estimate equilibrium and size controller hold-input without overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If large-lag positive-gain hypothesis is right, y will continue rising from ~0.44 toward ~0.53-0.58 over 120s with gradually declining but still positive end-slope (~0.0008-0.0012), staying well below soft limit and proving equilibrium for u=0.5 is above 0.5.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether output decays at u=0 and cooling time constant, which determines controller down-action and whether target can be held without oscillation.
experiments.expected_observation: If H4 positive-loss hypothesis is right, y will decay from ~0.54 toward ~0.20-0.30 over 180s with progressively slowing negative slope, still falling at end, confirming self-cooling and giving cooling time constant ~100-150s.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Linearity of steady-state gain and exact hold-input for y=0.5, which determines controller feedforward sizing.
experiments.expected_observation: If linear-gain hypothesis with Ya~0.08, K~0.92 and tau~120-150s is right, y will rise from ~0.23 toward ~0.49 steady state, reaching ~0.42-0.44 after 180s with still-positive end-slope ~0.0007-0.001, staying well below limits and confirming hold-input near 0.45-0.46.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Exact steady-state gain and equilibrium for u=0.45 by observing settling; this determines the feedforward hold-input for y=0.5 and validates linearity.
experiments.expected_observation: If linear first-order hypothesis with tau~110-150s and y_ss(0.45)~0.49-0.50 is right, y will rise from ~0.448 toward ~0.48-0.495 over 140s with declining but still slightly positive end-slope ~0.0003-0.0007, entering the lower edge of the 0.475-0.525 band and staying far below limits.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive gain).
Response has lag/time-constant of order 120-160s, settling takes ~300-400s, not instantaneous.
No large dead-zone: u=0.45 and u=0.5 produce rise clearly above noise.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward low ambient near 0.08.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u levels.
Steady-state u needed to hold y=0.5 is in mid-range [0.3,0.7], slightly below 0.5, near 0.43-0.44.
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) so trends are interpretable.
